ai_technology: Interpretable Bayesian network structure learning from molecular-dynamics interaction-energy time series

evidence.ai_role: Bayesian networks learned conditional dependencies among residue interaction-energy time series in active and inactive receptor simulations. Differences in learned network participation helped select a functionally coupled pocket for virtual screening and experimental compound testing.
evidence.tested: Screening of nine prioritized compounds identified Q2. Cellular signaling and radioligand assays, repeated in at least three experiments for key comparisons, showed altered agonist responses. Receptor mutations and G-protein-knockout tests supported the proposed allosteric interpretation; a six-receptor panel showed preferential, incomplete selectivity.
evidence.unknown: Q2 is an early low-affinity fragment with effects at high micromolar concentrations. Functional mutational effects do not independently prove its precise binding site or pose. Bootstrap stability was conditional on fixed inferred network topology. Generalization, independent replication, safety and therapeutic efficacy remain unestablished.

source_review.scope: Primary 47-page preprint PDF: relevant network construction and resampling Methods, screening and pharmacology Results, Table 1 and Discussion limitations; primary Research Square version metadata. Supplements not audited.

summary: A November 24, 2026 preprint reports that learned Bayesian networks of receptor dynamics helped prioritize an intracellular region of the angiotensin II type 1 receptor for compound screening. Laboratory signaling, radioligand and mutational tests supported a proposed negative allosteric effect of the resulting low-affinity fragment Q2. The experiments establish a bounded cellular pharmacology finding; they do not directly resolve the fragment’s binding pose or demonstrate therapeutic efficacy.
title: Learned receptor networks guide an experimentally tested AT1R modulator
